title: kiln.json
description: kiln.json is kiln's settings for a project, in .kiln/kiln.json. kiln reads them from main, never from a build's checkout, so a build cannot weaken its own gate.

$schema.description: $schema is the path of the JSON Schema that an editor checks this file against: "./kiln.schema.json". kiln init writes that schema beside this file. kiln ignores this key.

gate.description: gate lists the commands that must pass before work lands on main, such as ["go vet ./...", "go test ./..."]. kiln runs each with sh -c, from the top of a checkout of the work. kiln refuses a kiln.json that lists no command.

rounds.description: rounds is how many times kiln sends a build back to its session before the build stops, such as 3. kiln sends a build back when its gate fails, its work conflicts with main, or its work changes nothing. The audit's findings go back too, and use no round. Absent or 0, the first failing gate stops the build.

hosts.description: hosts lists the only hosts that a session's shell commands may connect to, such as ["proxy.golang.org", "*.example.org"]. Write each as a bare host name, with no scheme, port or path. Absent, those commands connect to no host.

writable.description: writable lists shell commands that print paths, such as ["go env GOCACHE GOMODCACHE"]. A session's shell commands may write to each printed path, as well as to the session's checkout. kiln runs each listed command with sh -c, and reads each word of its output as one absolute path. Absent, a session's commands write only to its checkout.

mcp.description: mcp lists the only MCP servers a session may call, by name, such as {"docs": {"command": "docs-mcp"}}. Write each server as Claude Code's mcpServers setting holds one. Each server runs outside the sandbox that confines a session's shell commands. Absent, a session calls no MCP server.

testSession.description: testSession, when true, gives each build two sessions. The build session writes the code. The verify session writes the acceptance tests from the spec alone. Neither session reads the other's checkout. Absent or false, one session writes the code and the tests. A build uses the value that main held when the build was queued.

acceptance.description: acceptance is the path that holds a spec's acceptance tests, such as "uat/{spec}/". kiln puts the spec's name in place of {spec}. A list of such paths gives each spec several paths. Each path names {spec} after a directory that no other listed path starts with. kiln queue refuses every spec while acceptance is absent. A build uses the value that main held when the build was queued.

shared.description: shared lists paths that the verify session may write besides the acceptance tests, such as ["internal/testutil/"]. Use it for helper code that the acceptance tests call, such as a test harness. The build session may write these paths too. Absent, the verify session writes only the acceptance tests and the spec's amendment file. kiln queue refuses a spec whose acceptance path equals, holds or lies under one of these paths. kiln ignores shared unless testSession is true. A build uses the value that main held when the build was queued.

reaudit.description: reaudit lists paths whose changes the audit must read before the work lands, such as ["migrations/"]. The audit reads the work once. When the work changes one of these paths after that, the audit reads the work again. That second reading uses a round. Absent, the audit never reads what a session changes in answer to the audit's findings.

notify.description: notify is a command that receives each notification, such as ".kiln/notify". A notification says that a build or a fix needs the developer. The command runs with sh -c, and reads the notification as JSON from the environment variable KILN_NOTICE. kiln kills a command that runs past 30 seconds. Absent, or when the command fails, kiln prints the notification as an OSC 9 escape sequence. A terminal shows that sequence as a desktop notification.

timeout.description: timeout is how long one command that kiln runs for the project may take, such as one gate command. It is also how long a session may print nothing. Past it, kiln kills that command or session. It does not limit a whole build. Write a Go duration above zero, such as "2h". Absent, it is 1 hour.
